saved_state_fix_contract.chosen_minimal_policy: Retain v1 and the current two-space JSON serialization format. Centralize the inclusive 1048576 UTF-8-byte limit and validate the actual normalized serialized string before writes/downloads. Do not silently switch formats, truncate fields or increase limits.
serialization: Validate the profile schema, serialize once using the chosen existing canonical format, then check TextEncoder byte length.
Expose a size-specific error distinguishable from schema failures and browser-storage errors.
Every ordinary successful export and successful save must round-trip through parseProfile/restoreProfile with equivalent normalized data.
import_transaction: Retain the existing raw-file byte, version and shape checks.
Before changing the live profile, undo state, selection or storage, also run bounded serialization on parsed/defaulted data.
If raw input fits but the normalized serialization exceeds the limit, reject the import with a normalization-size explanation and retain current state and stored bytes.

This deliberately adds a preflight at the extreme boundary; normal v1 data and the schema remain compatible. It must be documented instead of described as acceptance of every formerly parseable compact file.
If serialization passes but storage is unavailable, the imported description may stay in memory with an explicit unsaved status and working ordinary export.
save_and_export: Over-limit editing keeps the current in-memory description so the user can reduce notes, remove parts or deselect long custom language values.
Do not call setItem on a size/schema rejection; keep the previous valid saved value byte-for-byte.
Show that current edits are unsaved and how to reduce them. Do not advise ordinary export as recovery while ordinary export would fail the same limit.
Catch ordinary-export size errors before creating a Blob/download; emit no successful-export message.
A successful later reduction can save/export normally. Undo and structural edits must use the same save boundary.
Storage access/quota errors remain distinct from the size cap. No secondary backup key is required for this minimal fix.
unreadable_saved_value: Return a recovery state carrying the unreadable raw value and reason; the fallback profile may be edited in memory.
Pause all automatic writes to the affected key while that recovery state exists, including autosave after edits, undo or importing a valid replacement description.
Offer a clearly labeled recovery download of the retained raw value. It is evidence for recovery, not a supported system export, and may need external correction/reduction before import.
Only an explicit Replace saved system action may release protection. Preflight the new description, then write it; release the lock only after a successful write.
Downloading recovery data alone does not authorize replacement. Cancelling replacement, rejected imports and failed writes keep the raw value.
On a storage-read failure rather than known malformed raw data, keep saving unavailable until a successful read can establish the saved state; do not assume the key is empty.
Do not bypass the 1 MiB import policy to silently reinterpret or truncate oversized/unsupported raw data.
compatibility: Keep STORAGE_KEY='toolwiki.analysis-suite.v1', version=1, schema fields, count limits and legacy goals behavior.
Keep exact-boundary equality accepted and clarify user-facing wording as 'up to 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes)' rather than 'smaller than 1 MB'.
Do not require a storage migration or promise recovery of data already overwritten by old code.

A valid compact saved raw value can still be restored under the existing raw policy; if its next canonical save would exceed the cap, preserve that valid stored value and report the unsaved normalization limit.
